title: Reading Drill — Comparing protective cases for maps — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Comparing protective cases for maps — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The map conservator had been asked to investigate large maps rubbing against fasteners in storage in Bramley. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on new abrasion marks, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a nine-week comparison, the team used condition photographs at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because prior tears repaired with tape might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward pockets with a clear margin. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
